newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PNB drops 5.77 pct on peso weakness.
newsitem.headline: PNB drops 5.77 pct on peso weakness.

text.p: Shares of Philippine National Bank fell nine pesos, or 5.77 percent, to 147 pesos in early trade on Wednesday due to the negative effects of a weaker peso, brokers said.
"It is one bank with a large dollar denominated loan. If there's one bank that will go down with the peso depreciation story, that is PNB," said one broker.
PNB reached a low of 145 pesos earlier in the session.
"It's because of PNB's dollar loans. There's no other story," said Noel Reyes, vice-president at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Analysts also said PNB would be hurt by the current high interest rates, which would restrict its lending activities.
The central bank allowed the peso to float in a wider range last Friday. Prior to its move, the bank raised overnight rates to a 2-1/2 year high to defend the peso from speculation.

"If this interest rate environment persist, consumer financing will become prohibitive, loan growth will slow down and the banking sector will be adversely affected," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities Phils Inc.
PNB was one of the top ten most actively traded issues early in the session. Turnover was at 12.90 million pesos.
